nodes.author: bradmenezes
nodes.text:
I’m excited to introduce Clark, the first AI Agent to build internal enterprise apps.

We’ve raised $60M, including a fresh $23M from @sparkcapital @kleinerperkins, @MeritechCapital and Greenoaks.

Unlike consumer vibe coding tools like Lovable, Replit and Bolt that only generate prototypes, Clark builds production-ready internal apps — enforcing your enterprise standards:

🧩 UIs generated using your design system
🔌 Integrations with private APIs, databases and SaaS apps
🔐 Permissions mapped to @okta & @azuread  groups
🛡️ Security with audit logging, secrets management, and vulnerability scans

Clark is designed to operate exactly like a human internal tools team. It's built on a state-of-the-art multi-agent architecture, emulating your Designer, IT admin, Engineer, Security Operations, and QA employees.

When Clark generates an application, you can modify it in 3 ways:

1. Natural language - talk to Clark
2. Visual –  Edit it like in Figma
3. Code – Use your IDE like Cursor or VSCode

Global enterprises in regulated industries like @Instacart  (CART), @carrier  (CARR), and @cvent (Blackstone) already run their mission-critical apps on our platform.

Our customers save $5m on average. Book a demo and we'll save you $5m too. And we're so confident that if we can't, we'll donate $5,000 to a charity of your choice:

Book a Demo – http://www.superblocks.com/clark

---------

As part of this launch, we’re giving away the system prompts of leading AI products like Cursor, Manus, and Codex. 

These 6,000 line system prompts have enabled them to become billion-dollar companies on top of foundation models.

Retweet this post and comment ‘Superblocks’ below, and we'll send you the link so you can engineer world class prompts yourself.

👇 See Clark in action in the thread below

nodes.author: bradmenezes
nodes.text:
The industry is evolving from AI copilots to AI coworkers. 

Agents are able to autonomously take full tasks in the background. We’ve seen this just in the last few weeks from @OpenAI  Codex and @AnthropicAI  Claude Code. 

Every employee will have a team of AI agents working for them with most work being done asynchronous in the background – while you’re in a meeting and while you sleep. 

We built Clark to be your autonomous AI Coworker to build internal enterprise apps. 

Clark acts as a member of your internal tools team. He understands the context behind every task (e.g. design, IT, eng, security, QA, security) and ships mission-critical software that follows your enterprise standards. 

Let’s see an example of Clark in action:

In this demo, Jordan, a Senior Sales Engineer at @superblocks, assigns a Jira ticket to Clark:

 📝 “Build a Command Center app to manage call center interactions.”

Clark responds right in the Jira thread: acknowledging the task, outlining his approach, and getting to work.

A few minutes later, the full app is built, complete with a staging link for review from deploying to prod. Even better, all enterprise standards are applied automatically:

 ✅ Design system
 ✅ RBAC + SSO
 ✅ Audit logging
 ✅ Secure integrations 

Need to tweak something?
→  Use the drag-and-drop Visual Builder 
→  Extend with code in your IDE
→  Or simply reply to Clark in the Jira ticket itself 

The best part is that you can assign 10 Jira tickets to Clark and Superblocks will spin up agents for each of them in parallel scaling your workforce and empowering employees to do more. 

This is what it looks like when AI becomes a real teammate, not just a copilot. 

And when that happens, you unlock a whole new class of builders to ship 10-100x more internal software, securely and sustainably, alongside engineering and IT.

Clark is currently in private preview. Sign up for early access at the link in the comments.

nodes.author: RaulJuncoV
nodes.text:
I was bored building internal tools... until I discovered this.

Every internal CRUD app felt like déjà vu.

Auth. Forms. Table views. Wiring databases.
Week after week, of rebuilding the same thing in slightly different ways.

It’s not that the work was hard; it was just... uninspiring.

Then I stumbled on a platform that changed how I think about internal tools.

With Superblocks, you can stitch together real apps fast.
Not no-code fluff. Real APIs. Real logic. Real control.

What surprised me most?
It feels like coding, but without the repetitive scaffolding.
